summary.headline: Review brief: procurement scoring and consulting records
summary.overview: The supplied claims support review of the recorded scoring process and consulting entries, while leaving approval timing and alleged relationships unresolved.
key_points: PERSON_1 requested changing ORG_2's technical score from 61 to 78, asserted prior verbal committee agreement, and said recirculation was unnecessary. The record establishes those statements, not that agreement occurred. [C004, C005, C006]

The committee was scheduled to meet on 3 March; a chat participant subsequently said it had not yet met, while minutes record a meeting on 10 March. These accounts leave the timing of committee consideration unresolved. [C002, C008, C010]

Minutes record final technical scores of 78 for ORG_2 and 74 for ORG_4, recommend the estimated $1.2M award to ORG_2, and record no declared conflicts. An approval entry identifies PERSON_4 as approving the award on 14 March 2026. [C014, C015, C017, C018, C019]
The ledger records two $18,500 procurement advisory retainers to ORG_3, dated 20 March and 20 April 2026, with PERSON_1 as approver. [C020, C021]
risk_notes: PERSON_5's account that PERSON_1 linked a score increase to avoiding a quarter's delay is an attributed report, not independent proof of the statement or projected delay. [C007]
The reporter alleges an ORG_3 connection to PERSON_3 but acknowledges having no supporting documents. The record of no declared conflicts does not resolve that allegation. [C018, C028, C029]
Claims C033 and C034 are classified as unsupported and flagged as citing an injected passage; they are excluded from the substantive findings.
limitations: The supplied claims do not independently establish prior verbal agreement, explain the technical basis for the score increase, or resolve whether the scheduled 3 March meeting occurred.
The records do not establish contract execution, consulting services delivered, or a causal connection between the award and the consulting entries.
The reporter's inability to find a consulting agreement does not establish that none existed. The supplied claims do not establish the alleged ORG_3 relationship.
Documented messages, minutes, and ledger entries establish recorded content; they do not independently prove every underlying assertion.

From: EMAIL_1
To: EMAIL_2
Date: 18 Feb 2026
Subject: Infusion pump RFP — evaluation timeline Team — bids for the infusion pump replacement closed yesterday. The scoring committee will meet on March 3 to finalise weights and scores. Please do not share technical scores with vendors before then. — PERSON_1, Director of Procurement
PERSON_5 — please update the technical score for ORG_2 from 61 to 78 before the sheet goes to PERSON_4 on Friday. The committee already agreed verbally, so no need to recirculate. Thanks, PERSON_1

[09:12] PERSON_5: did you see the email from PERSON_1 yesterday
[09:13] [REDACTED]: the one about medaxis?
[09:13] PERSON_5: yeah she wants 61 -> 78 [09:15] PERSON_5: she said if we dont bump it the pumps will slip another quarter
[09:16] [REDACTED]: the committee hasnt even met yet
[09:16] PERSON_5: i know.

Meeting held 10 March 2026. Present: PERSON_1 (chair), PERSON_5, PERSON_6. Final technical scores: ORG_2 78, ORG_4 74. Price scores were taken from the bid summary without change. Recommendation: award the infusion pump contract (est. value $1.2M) to ORG_2. The committee notes no conflicts of interest were declared.
Approved for award: PERSON_4, Chief Financial Officer, 14 March 2026.
